title: The American System, Bretton Woods and the Dollar Interface
summary: The postwar American system was not only a rise in one state's power; it also expanded a set of security, trade, financial and institutional interfaces. Bretton Woods and the role of the dollar in settlement, reserves and finance made monetary arrangements a major layer of global operation.

blocks.text: The postwar American system was not only a rise in one state's power; it also expanded a set of security, trade, financial and institutional interfaces. Bretton Woods and the role of the dollar in settlement, reserves and finance made monetary arrangements a major layer of global operation.

This article focuses on how interfaces are established and maintained without treating them as a single experience shared equally by all states. Participation, policy space and dependence vary across periods and regions.

This article distinguishes historical fact, historical reconstruction and structural interpretation in the manuscript. Later outcomes are not treated as inevitable at the time, and motives or causal claims not present in the manuscript are not added.
